agent AGENTS.md api app bootstrap.sh CLAUDE.md docs package-lock.json package.json README.md scripts skills-lock.json team-setup tmp vercel.json # DelayedBahn — error404.ai Share your train trip, and delayedBahn tells you how late each train is likely to be and whether you will make your change. It learns from Deutsche Bahn's own timetable and delay data. Built by team error404.ai at the European Hackathon League Zurich. ![Demo](docs/images/demo.png) ## Contents 1. [Problem](#problem) 2. [What we built](#what-we-built) 3. [The app](#the-app) 4. [Data](#data) 5. [What the DB data solves](#what-the-db-data-solves) 6. [Architecture](#architecture) 7. [Model](#model) 8. [Approach: two methods, combined](#approach-two-methods-combined) 9. [Evaluation](#evaluation) 10. [Code structure](#code-structure) 11. [Quickstart](#quickstart) 12. [Team](#team) 13. [Built with](#built-with) 14. [Screenshots](#screenshots) --- ## Problem - Everyone who travels with Deutsche Bahn knows the situation: trains are late and connections break. - The DB app shows the planned journey, not the chance that it actually works. - We cannot fix delays for everyone. But we can give each of our travellers a more reliable and comfortable journey, and that is where the app comes in. ## What we built - **Share a trip** from the DB app into our web app. It reads the trains, stations and times. - **Get a forecast per train**: likely arrival delay, a range, and the chance of making each change. - **Get advice**: the plan is fine, add buffer, or take an earlier or later connection. ## The app - **Start screen:** paste the text you copied from the DB app, or share it straight from your phone. The app can be installed on your home screen. - **Map:** your route drawn on a map of Germany, with the trains moving along it. - **Train cards:** one card per train with the likely delay, the range, and a short explanation from the model. - **Advice:** a clear verdict for the whole trip, and other options if a change looks tight. --- ## Data ### Sources All product data comes from Deutsche Bahn's official API Marketplace. | API | What we use it for | Endpoints | Auth | |---|---|---|---| | [Timetables](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/timetables) | Planned stops, live delays, cancellations, platform changes, route of every train | `station/{name}`, `plan/{eva}/{date}/{hour}`, `fchg/{eva}` | `DB_CLIENT_ID`, `DB_API_KEY` | | [RIS::Stations](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/ris-stations) | Official station names and EVA numbers | `stop-places/by-key` | Same keys | - **Historic DB data:** stored responses from the same Timetables feeds, one row per train per stop, published as [`piebro/deutsche-bahn-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/piebro/deutsche-bahn-data). The model is trained on this. - **Live DB data:** fetched from the APIs when a traveller shares a trip (`scripts/db_live_extract.py`, `trip/live.py`). ### Agentic retrieval pipeline - **Search:** an agent looks for data sources that could help explain delays (`db_route/discover/`). - **Decide:** it proposes which sources and which columns to keep, and which to drop. Every decision is then checked by fixed rules in code. - **Clean:** noise and irrelevant data are filtered out, so the model gets clean input that can be explained. - **Combine:** historic DB data and live DB data end up in the same format for the model. ## What the DB data solves | Traveller problem | DB data that answers it | |---|---| | "Which train and station is this?" | Timetables `station` lookup and RIS::Stations turn names from the share text into exact station IDs | | "Is my train late right now?" | The Timetables change feed (`fchg`) gives the current delay at every stop the train has passed | | "Will it get worse before my stop?" | Planned route and stops ahead, plus how earlier trains on the same line did today | | "Is this station having a bad day?" | Late share across all trains at the station recently | | "Will this train be cancelled?" | Cancellation flags in the change feed, and how often this route was cancelled before | | "Will I make my change?" | Planned arrival and departure times of both trains, combined with both delay forecasts | --- ## Architecture ```mermaid graph TD A["Live DB data
today's delays from Timetables + RIS::Stations"] --> P["Agentic retrieval pipeline
keeps what helps, drops noise"] B["Historic DB data
past delays, every train, every stop"] --> P P --> C["Delay model
fine-tuned Llama 3.2"] C --> D["Web app
shared trip in, forecast out"] ``` 1. **Collect:** we read timetables and delays from the DB APIs. 2. **Clean:** the retrieval pipeline keeps the useful data and drops the noise. 3. **Learn:** the model learns how delays grow along a trip from historic records. 4. **Predict:** when you share a trip, the app sends it to the model together with today's live delays and shows you the forecast. ## Model - **Base model:** Llama 3.2, an open-source language model, fine-tuned on historic DB data with LoRA. - **Time series support:** built with [OpenTSLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02410), so the model can read time series next to text. - **Input:** for one train and one stop it is heading to, the delays so far on this trip, how earlier trains to that stop did, and the recent lateness of the station. - **Output:** the most likely delay in minutes, a range, and the chance of cancellation. - **Connections:** the chance of making a change comes from the two trains' forecasts and the planned transfer time (`trip/connection.py`). ## Approach: two methods, combined The model can take the same delay history in two ways (`--prompt-mode` in `trip/train.py`): - **Time-series embeddings:** the delay series go through a time-series encoder, which turns them into embeddings the language model reads directly. - **Pure text:** the same numbers are written into the prompt as text, together with a short sentence that describes them. - **Combined:** both at once, embeddings plus text. Each method is an existing tool on its own. The idea is to combine them. We train each one separately and then the combination, so the comparison shows what each part adds: text only, embeddings only, and embeddings plus text. ## Evaluation - **Baseline:** the model is compared against simple and statistical baselines built on the same information (`trip/baselines.py`). - **Split:** data is split by time. The model is tested on a later period it never saw during training, so no future information leaks into training. --- ## Code structure ``` api/ Vercel entry: sends /api/* to the backend app/backend/ Node API (no dependencies): parse share text, predict, recommend app/frontend/ React web app: paste or share a trip, forecast, advice, map app/agents/ Python: data pipeline, model training, model server src/features/db_delay/trip/ the delay model (build, train, serve) src/features/db_route/discover/ agentic retrieval pipeline src/features/db_route/ route-level delay experiments scripts/ DB Timetables and RIS::Stations clients team-setup/ team coordination: tasks, decisions, hooks bootstrap.sh local setup check ``` | File | What it does | |---|---| | `scripts/db_live_extract.py` | Calls Timetables and RIS::Stations, merges plan and changes into one row per train per stop | | `app/agents/src/features/db_route/discover/run.py` | Runs the retrieval pipeline: search, assess, probe sources | | `app/backend/src/features/share-parser/grammar.js` | Reads DB share text into a journey (`POST /api/journeys/parse`) | | `app/backend/src/features/delay-prediction/routes/delay-prediction.js` | Asks the model for each train, works out change risk (`POST /api/predict`) | | `app/backend/src/features/recommendation/routes/recommendation.js` | Gives the verdict and alternatives (`POST /api/recommend`) | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/build.py` | Turns stop records into training examples | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/train.py` | Fine-tunes the model in text, embedding or combined mode | | `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/serve.py` | Serves forecasts to the backend, using live Timetables data | --- ## Quickstart ```bash git clone https://github.com/KiraKami-dev/temporal_ai_error404.ai.git cd temporal_ai_error404.ai cp .env.example .env # add DB_CLIENT_ID and DB_API_KEY from developers.deutschebahn.com ln -s ../../.env app/backend/.env python3 scripts/db_timetables.py "Hamburg Hbf" # live departures from DB cd app/backend && npm run dev # terminal 1: API on http://localhost:8000 npm --prefix app/frontend ci && npm --prefix app/frontend run dev # terminal 2, repo root: app on http://127.0.0.1:5173 ``` To run the trained model locally, see "Model files (required)" in `app/agents/src/features/db_delay/trip/README.md`. ## Team error404.ai — Akshat Khair, Gaurav Kulkarni, Jonas (`josteng`), Yash (`yash-epte`) ## Built with - European Hackathon League Zurich - Deutsche Bahn API Marketplace: [Timetables](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/timetables), [RIS::Stations](https://developers.deutschebahn.com/db-api-marketplace/apis/product/ris-stations) - [OpenTSLM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.02410), Llama 3.2, Nebius GPUs --- ## Screenshots ![App](docs/images/demo.png) ![Data extraction code](docs/images/code_data.png) ![Model training code](docs/images/code_model.png) ![Example run](docs/images/example.png) ---- # AGENTS.md — hack-os shared agent instructions Single source of truth for every coding harness. `CLAUDE.md` points here. Read this whole file once per session. These rules govern product work; explicitly requested maintenance of hack-os itself is not constrained by an example product's demo script or contract. ## 1. Boot sequence and freshness If `.hackos-user` is absent, run `./bootstrap.sh --auto` once. Bootstrap is local-only: no downloads, product dependency installs, git config changes, or credentials. Missing tools warn; markdown remains usable. Identity not matched to the roster is unconfirmed: ask the human, never assume ownership. MCP authentication and personal API keys are optional, per-person setup. Read `team-setup/state/event.json` first. `mode: example`, or a legacy `_comment` containing `WORKED EXAMPLE` without an explicit mode, means NO active event. Say "No active event; fictional examples are inactive." A blank `event_name` also means no active event, regardless of mode; report "No event configured" and do not load placeholder state as requirements. Do not load fictional challenges, contracts, owners, tasks, or decisions as requirements. Never silently initialize or reset an event. The distributed template keeps event records and shared session logs empty. Keep the reusable roster in `team.json`; assign product roles fresh per event. For an active event, read in order: 1. `team-setup/state/pipeline.json` 2. `team-setup/state/decisions.md` — identify current, non-superseded decisions. 3. `team-setup/state/owners.md` 4. `team-setup/board/tasks.json` — identify the relevant task and accountable owner. 5. `team-setup/state/01-challenge-pick/challenge.md` 6. `team-setup/state/02-demo-script/demo-script.md` 7. `team-setup/state/02-demo-script/not-building.md` 8. `team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md` Load `ideas.md`, `research.json`, and supporting notes when relevant. Any document marked `WORKED EXAMPLE` is illustrative, never active scope. State the active stage, your confirmed ownership, current task/decisions, and whether the real contract is frozen. Missing information is unknown, not permission to invent assignments or implement fictional requirements. Before a new task or substantial edit, reread decisions, ownership, the relevant task and contract. After a teammate reports a change, refresh even in a running session. A dashboard refresh does not refresh an agent's mind. Git is explicit synchronization, not live collaboration. `event.json` names the coordination branch and maintainer. The maintainer integrates accepted state changes there; teammates fetch and safely integrate before new work and at checkpoints. Never auto-pull into a dirty worktree, discard changes, auto-stash, or resolve another person's conflicts. Show local HEAD, uncommitted coordination edits, and remote freshness as unknown until checked. Offline work uses a local snapshot, never a claimed live team state. ## 2. Hackathon mode - Write smoke tests for the demo happy path and coordination data safety. - Do not add unit tests for unrelated product code or refactor working code. - No speculative abstractions, new dashboards, providers, or services. - Core storage/API stays Python 3 stdlib plus Git. The dashboard UI uses Vite, React, Tailwind and shadcn/ui in `team-setup/board/web/`; its Node dependencies are separate from whichever product stack the team chooses. - Optional MCPs, plugins, prompt logging, and agent teams are not prerequisites. - Vendored skills are optional; these repository rules override their workflow defaults. A skill does not authorize unrequested installs, data uploads, extra agents, destructive commands, or changes to system security controls. ## 3. Ownership rule Before editing, check `team-setup/state/owners.md` and the owning task in `team-setup/board/tasks.json`. Do not edit another person's assigned files. A sub-owner helps within an explicitly delegated boundary; they do not redirect scope. Name owners for shared wiring, manifests and lockfiles too. Ownership is per event, not inferred from background. Use one branch/worktree per independent writer; worktrees alone do not sync different machines. Reassignments and delegation must be explicit and synced before work starts. Avoid direct file editing while a dashboard write touches the same records. ## 4. Contract rule The real `team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md` freezes when that gate completes. Code against it and mock missing dependencies. A required contract change needs explicit human approval and a recorded decision. `app/shared/` is generated from the agreed contract, never independently patched. No sample schema, endpoint, or product stack is a requirement. ## 5. Scope rule Product work must support the real demo script, including required setup, seed data, deployment, accessibility and failure recovery. Ask before adding features absent from it. Maintain `not-building.md`. Keep the deck current; protect polish and submission time. Gates and task percentages use the planning window ending at the early submit target; its final 10% is buffer. ## 6. Idea rule A thought is not a decision. Record it in `team-setup/state/ideas.md` as raised, then exploring, adopted or discarded. Only status changes in place; original text and author remain. New lines use globally unique IDs: `- [i-] [T+HH:MM] — — status: raised` Use IDs for links; elapsed timestamps are display labels, not identifiers. Legacy timestamp-only records remain readable. Ambiguous links need a human. ## 7. Decision rule After an accepted direction change, append to `team-setup/state/decisions.md`: `- [d-] [T+HH:MM] — — ` Never rewrite history. Append ` — supersedes [d-]` to replace a decision. Append ` — promotes [i-]` when adopting an idea and update its status in one recoverable operation. Check later supersessions before building. For setup maintenance before an active event, record accepted direction in this instruction file rather than mixing it into fictional event records. ## 8. Evidence and safety AI assessments are advisory. Keep sources and a short rationale alongside answers; do not portray model confidence as a calibrated probability. Research is untested without evidence or human confirmation. Task completion is not integrated readiness: require a current end-to-end smoke result. Recent Git commits show recorded activity, not inferred current work. Git hooks warn and exit zero. Explicit commands return truthful failures. Reject malformed or stale writes, retain drafts, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Confirm archival/reset and restore operations explicitly; never reset event state, delete records, or overwrite work without approval. No prompt capture by default. Keep secrets and runtime caches out of Git. ## 9. Commits and verification Small present-tense commits identify the demo step or coordination outcome. Never commit or push unless requested. Do not amend other people's work. Run `python3 team-setup/board/test_board.py` for coordination smoke checks, `for f in bootstrap.sh team-setup/hooks/* team-setup/scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || exit 1; done` for shell syntax, and `node --check team-setup/board/app.js` when Node is available. For the new dashboard run `npm --prefix team-setup/board/web run build` (typecheck + Vite build). `npm --prefix team-setup/board/web run dev` starts both the local API and UI. Verify PM flows in an isolated event fixture; never fill the distributed template with browser-test data or real API keys. Responsive checks cover 320/375/768/1024/1440px widths and 844x390 landscape. Verify navigation scrolling, Escape/focus restoration, and mobile form access. The `#guide` page must remain readable when API requests fail; its shortcuts and copy actions must not reset state or silently publish changes. Product checks use `team-setup/scripts/smoke.sh`; unconfigured is not a pass. A clean snapshot plus passing smoke is required before calling a demo ready. This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification. @.entire/graph-agent.md

### Model files (required)

The checkpoint and the data around it are not in Git. Running the model locally needs three files:

| File | Size | Where it comes from |
|---|---|---|
| `checkpoint.pt` | 102 MB | The shipped embedding model, split mode on the v7 data after 6,000 steps (long delay history, same-train gains and corridor series through the time-series encoder): bucket key `models/db-trip-delay-v7-split-6k.pt` (`nebius/sync_bucket.sh get`, S3 keys in the root `.env`), or `checkpoint.pt` in the team's `delayedBahn-model.zip`. The submitted text model, `models/db-trip-delay-final.pt`, runs with `PROMPT_MODE=text` |
| `september_v7_test.parquet` | 11 MB | Recorded September trips with the v7 features: the recorded journeys and the stored history of live forecasts; in the zip |
| `xgb/` (`quantile.json`, `late.json`, `cancel.json`, `features.json`) | 218 MB | The refitted statistical forecast the v7 prompt reads; in the zip, or refitted at setup from `examples_v7.parquet` (bucket key `data/examples_v7.parquet`) in about 3 minutes |

The zip also carries `INSTRUCTIONS.md` with these steps. The base model (Llama 3.2 3B) and the
OpenTSLM start checkpoint download from Hugging Face during setup, about 7 GB. Setup puts
everything into one folder, kept separate from the unpacked files because it copies the checkpoint:

```
<dir>/.venv/                        Python 3.12 environment (torch with MPS, OpenTSLM, xgboost)
<dir>/model/checkpoint.pt           the model
<dir>/data/september_test.parquet   the recorded trips
<dir>/xgb/                          the statistical forecast; without it there is no live data
```

```bash
# with the ready xgb/ folder from the zip
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <files>/checkpoint.pt <files>/september_v7_test.parquet
cp -R <files>/xgb <dir>/xgb
# or refit it from the training examples
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <files>/checkpoint.pt <files>/september_v7_test.parquet examples_v7.parquet
```

Live data also needs `DB_CLIENT_ID` and `DB_API_KEY` (DB API Marketplace, Timetables API, free
plan) in the repo root `.env`, passed as `ENV_FILE` to `start`.

### Live on a laptop (Apple silicon)

The 3B model fits an Apple silicon laptop: `run_local.sh` builds the environment, then serves a
checkpoint live on MPS and starts the team backend and PWA in front of it. Forecasts are computed
for any recorded September trip, not only for saved ones.

```bash
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> db-trip-delay-v7-split-6k.pt september_v7_test.parquet
trip/run_local.sh start <dir>    # model on :8502, app on http://localhost:8000
```

Checked: v7 text on MPS reproduces the H100's saved test forecasts (same median and 10 to 90%
range on the sampled trips, distributions within bf16 noise), loads in a few seconds and answers
a two-leg journey in about two seconds. For an unstacked checkpoint such as final-v2-text, pass
`DROP_XGB=1` at setup so its prompt has no XGBoost sentence.

### Live DB data

With the statistical forecast refitted once (`live_xgb.py`, same features and settings as
`baselines.py`; it reproduces the September `xgb_*` columns with correlation 0.999), `serve.py
--xgb` answers legs that have no recorded trip from the DB Timetables API (`live.py`, reusing the
client and plan/change merge of `scripts/db_live_extract.py`). The row follows `build.py` at
t0 = now:

| Input | Source |
|---|---|
| Run delays (origin and the 4 stops before boarding), previous trains at the target (6 h), corridor trains (3 h), the target's last 3 hours | Live: `plan` per station hour, `fchg` per station |
| 90-day history at the target, same train number's earlier days | Latest stored rows (September scrape) |
| Older station hours, nationwide hours | Stored, filled by hour of day |
| `xgb_*` | Refitted XGBoost-v7 on the assembled row |

A cold leg costs 15 to 40 calls (station lookups and plan hours cached for the process, change
feeds for a minute), so one key at 60 calls per minute serves about two new legs per minute. The
nationwide and multi-day inputs need a collector over all ~5,300 stations (about 3 keys at the
archive's cadence) or the public archive to become fully live.

```bash
trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <checkpoint.pt> september_v7_test.parquet examples_v7.parquet
ENV_FILE=<repo root>/.env trip/run_local.sh start <dir>
```

Checked: a real two-leg journey planned for the next half hour through `POST /api/predict` on the
team backend, answered in 9 seconds with 22 API calls per leg and no fallback.

### When DB live data fails

`serve.py` answers every leg, trying in this order:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a trip-delay checkpoint live on an Apple silicon laptop (MPS) behind the team app.
# The model files (checkpoint, September rows, xgb/) are not in Git: see "Model files" in trip/README.md.
#
#   trip/run_local.sh setup <dir> <checkpoint.pt> <september test parquet> [<training examples parquet>]
#   trip/run_local.sh start <dir>
#
# setup builds a Python 3.12 environment in <dir> (the training pins minus the CUDA packages, plus
# xgboost), caches the base model and the OpenTSLM start checkpoint, copies the checkpoint and the
# September rows, and builds the PWA. With the training examples it also refits the statistical
# forecast once (live_xgb.py), which live examples need. start serves the model on MODEL_PORT
# (default 8502) and the team backend with the PWA on PORT (default 8000).
#
# Live data: when <dir>/xgb exists, legs without a recorded trip are built from the DB Timetables
# API (live.py) with DB_CLIENT_ID and DB_API_KEY from ENV_FILE (default: the repo root's .env),
# at most CALLS_PER_MINUTE (default 55) calls per minute.
#
# Default: the embedding model, split mode on v7 after 6k steps (bucket key models/db-trip-delay-v7-split-6k.pt) with
# september_v7_test.parquet. Its prompt carries XGBoost's forecast, so the xgb_* columns stay.
# For an unstacked model such as final-v2-text, set DROP_XGB=1 at setup so its prompt matches

## Option A: full app with the real model (what you ran yesterday)

```bash

content.text:
No, that's not intended. The map only draws trains whose route it can place, and on your trip two of the three touch **Buchloe**, which has no coordinates.

**Why it happens**

1. **Buchloe isn't in the station tables.** Coordinates come only from hand-made lists: 48 stations in `app/frontend/src/lib/stations.json` and 58 in `app/backend/src/features/share-parser/fixtures/stations.json`. Buchloe is in neither. The backend's DB lookup (`stations.js`) still finds Buchloe, but it only returns the EVA number and name. I checked with the real keys: Zürich HB, Augsburg Hbf and Erlangen come back with lat/lon, and Buchloe comes back as `{"evaNumber":"8000057","name":"Buchloe"}` with none.
2. **The route-shape fallbacks don't work for it either.** The rail router and OSM matching need coordinates at both ends. The only other source is the online timetable service, v6.db.transport.rest, which returned HTTP 503 when I tried it.
3. **The map skips those legs without saying so.** `legLine()` returns nothing for them, so `drawRoute` leaves out EC 199 (Zürich HB → Buchloe) and train 2 (Buchloe → Augsburg). The camera fit ignores them too, which leaves only Augsburg → Erlangen. That's also why picking "train 1 / 3" doesn't move the map: `flyToLeg` has no area to zoom to and does nothing.

The forecasts aren't affected: the model works with EVA numbers, not coordinates. Only the map is.

**Ways to fix it**

- **For the screenshot, quickest:** add Buchloe to both station tables with its official coordinates. All three trains would then draw.
- **Proper fix:** when a station isn't in the table, have the backend fetch its coordinates from RIS::Stations. The team already uses that API and the keys are in `.env`. Any German station would then show up on the map.
- **Optional:** show a short note such as "1 train can't be drawn on the map" instead of hiding it silently.

I haven't changed anything. I can do the quick fix now, or the RIS::Stations one if you'd rather have it work for any trip.

content.text:
I fixed it: stations missing from the local table now get map coordinates, so the Buchloe trains will be drawn. It works locally; the site on your phone needs a deploy first.

**What changed:** in `app/backend/src/features/share-parser/stations.js`, when the DB lookup finds a station but no coordinates, the backend now looks them up by its EVA number:
1. **RIS::Stations first.** The team's DB keys aren't subscribed to it: it returned **401 "Cannot find valid subscription"** even with the correct media type. After a 401 the backend stops trying RIS until restart. Subscribing the DB app to RIS::Stations in the Marketplace would switch it on with no code change.
2. **OpenStreetMap as the fallback.** It matches the station by EVA number (OSM's `uic_ref` tag) and needs no key. For Buchloe it gives lat 48.0333, lon 10.7161.
3. **Cache.** Only lookups that succeed are cached, so a dropped connection on the train can't hide a station until the next restart.

The frontend didn't need changes: once both ends have coordinates, the map's existing route drawing works. I checked that brouter.de draws Zürich HB → Buchloe as 259 km of track.

**Checks:**
- **Tests:** all 60 backend tests pass, including a new one for the RIS path, the OSM fallback and the cache.
- **Live lookup:** Buchloe resolves with coordinates in about 2.3 s the first time and instantly from cache.
- **Running app:** I restarted it and sent a made-up Zürich HB → Buchloe → Augsburg Hbf share text to `POST /api/journeys/parse`. Both legs came back with coordinates at every station. It's running again at http://localhost:8000.
- **Not checked:** I haven't looked at the drawn map in a browser.

**Where it lives:**
- **Commit:** `279e195` "Give unknown stations map coordinates" on `main`, covering `stations.js`, its test file and the share-parser README. Not pushed.
- **Background job:** the app now runs as `b34llywr9`; output goes to `../local-model-env/run_local.log`.

**For the LinkedIn screenshot:** your phone screenshot looks like it came from the Vercel site, and that runs the same backend code as the local app. It will show all three trains only after this commit is pushed and deployed. If you'd rather not deploy, share the trip into http://localhost:8000 on your laptop now. Should I push `main`?

And why is it at first before scrolling sometimes straight lines and not the train lines. That should also be fixed.

You're asking for two things on the phone map:
1. **Labels:** place station names and delay badges so they're visible on the first screen, next to their station. They should avoid the screen edge, the map buttons, the bottom sheet, the route line and each other; for example Augsburg/Buchloe could sit below or to the left.
2. **Straight lines:** the route sometimes shows straight lines instead of track lines until you scroll.

`app/frontend` is Akshat's area in `owners.md`; since you asked for these changes directly, I'll go ahead and mention it at the end. First I'll find where the station labels and delay badges are created and how the route gets redrawn when track shapes arrive.

25	export function goHome(map: maplibregl.Map) {

32	export function fitJourney(map: maplibregl.Map, journeys: Journey[], opts: { maxZoom?: number; duration?: number } = {}) {
33	  let minLon = Infinity, minLat = Infinity, maxLon = -Infinity, maxLat = -Infinity
34	  for (const j of journeys) {
35	    const b = journeyBounds(j)
36	    if (!b) continue
37	    minLon = Math.min(minLon, b[0][0]); minLat = Math.min(minLat, b[0][1])
38	    maxLon = Math.max(maxLon, b[1][0]); maxLat = Math.max(maxLat, b[1][1])
39	  }
40	  if (!isFinite(minLon)) return
41	  // Give very short routes some air so the fit does not zoom to street level.
42	  const padDeg = 0.02
43	  map.setPadding({ top: 0, bottom: 0, left: 0, right: 0 })
44	  map.fitBounds(
45	    [
46	      [minLon - padDeg, minLat - padDeg],
47	      [maxLon + padDeg, maxLat + padDeg],
48	    ],
49	    { padding: panelPadding(), duration: opts.duration ?? dur(DUR.fly), maxZoom: opts.maxZoom ?? 10.5, pitch: motionOff() ? 0 : 48, bearing: 0, essential: true },
50	  )
51	}

61	      [bounds[1][0] + padDeg, bounds[1][1] + padDeg],
62	    ],
63	    { padding: panelPadding(), duration: dur(1600), maxZoom: 11.5, pitch: motionOff() ? 0 : 35, essential: true },
64	  )

  page.on('pageerror', e => log.push(`${at()} PAGEERROR ${e.message.slice(0, 200)}`))
  await page.goto('http://localhost:8000/')
  await page.locator('textarea').fill(text)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /Check my (trip|plan)/ }).click()
  await page.waitForTimeout(15000)
  const state = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    canvas: document.querySelectorAll('.maplibregl-canvas').length,
    mapRoot: document.querySelectorAll('.map-root').length,
    placeholder: document.querySelector('.map-placeholder')?.textContent?.slice(0, 60) ?? null,
    sheet: document.querySelector('.travel-sheet h2')?.textContent ?? null,
    markers: document.querySelectorAll('.station-marker').length,
    controls: document.querySelectorAll('.map-controls button').length,
  }))
  console.log(`run ${run}:`, JSON.stringify(state))
  for (const line of log.filter(l => !/GPU stall|GL Driver/.test(l))) console.log('   ', line)
  await ctx.close()
}
await browser.close()
EOF

Both fixes are in and committed; the running app at http://localhost:8000 already serves the new build.

**Labels.** Each station's name and forecast badge are now one block that stays next to its dot. The code tries 12 positions around the dot: the four sides, the four diagonals, and slid up or down on the left and right. It picks the one that avoids, in order of priority:
- going off-screen or under the map buttons or the bottom sheet
- covering another label or another station's dot
- covering the route line

It re-checks while the map moves, on resize, and when the forecasts arrive, and it only switches sides when the new spot is clearly better, so labels don't flicker.

**Straight lines.** The map was waiting for transport.rest, which currently fails after a 6 s timeout, even though the rail router already had the tracks after about 3 s. Now each leg switches to its track as soon as any source answers, and a better source still replaces it later. Upgrading a trip that's already on the map no longer replays the draw-in animation.

**Checks** (headless Chromium, same four-station trip as your screenshot):
- **Phone (390×844):** all four stations and forecasts are visible on the first screen, with no overlaps and nothing under the buttons or sheet. One leftover: Buchloe's badge covers a short piece of the Zürich–Buchloe track.
- **Desktop (1440×900):** labels sit to the right of their dots, off the route.
- **Timing:** before, straight lines stayed until 7.9 s; now the tracks drew in the first draw (4.3–4.7 s), with no straight-line phase.
- **Build:** the typecheck and build pass.
- **Smoke tests:** 12 of the 14 tests in `traveler.smoke.mjs` fail, but they were already broken before my changes. They wait for UI that no longer exists in the committed code, such as "Your connection outlook", "How it works" and a missing `JourneyBuilder.tsx`. The suite needs updating separately.
- **Not checked:** only this one trip; no other trips or a real phone.

- Two headless runs failed while your connection was down. Without the basemap the map never finishes loading, so it shows no route at all. That was already the case and I didn't change it.

# Using Entire

Your default when exploring or understanding code should be: **read the
recorded intent, don't guess.**

Entire checkpoints capture the prompts, transcripts, and decisions behind every
agent-driven change. When you need to understand why code exists or how a module
evolved, look up the checkpoint history first. Only fall back to inference from
code structure when no history is available — and label that explicitly.

## When This Skill Activates

Use this skill whenever the task involves:

- A request phrased as "research X", "investigate X", "look into X", "dig into
  X", or "find out how X works"
- Exploring or understanding an unfamiliar module or file
- Preparing to refactor, extend, or debug code you didn't write
- Answering "why is this like this?" or "what was the intent?"
- Doing pre-work research before making changes
- Any codebase exploration where historical context would help

For a research- or investigate-shaped request, the very first action is an
`entire search` via the `search` skill. Do not open source files or grep first;
the recorded history says what was tried and why, and code reads come after to
confirm it.

Do **not** use this skill for simple, well-understood edits where you already
have full context (e.g. "add a comment to line 5").

## First Step: Check Repository Status

Before diving into specific lookups, check whether Entire is available and
the repository has checkpoint history:

```bash
entire status
```

This tells you whether Entire is enabled, which git hooks are installed, whether
the metadata branch is initialized, and any active sessions on the current
branch.

## Scenario Routing

When this skill activates, determine which sub-skill best fits the user's need:

| Scenario | Typical user expressions | Delegate to |
|----------|------------------------|-------------|
| Code block provenance | "why is this like this" / "wtf is going on" / "what happened at src/auth.ts:42" / "tell me why this changed" | `what-happened` |
| Research or investigate a topic | "research X" / "investigate X" / "look into X" / "dig into X" / "what do we know about X" | `search` first, then this skill's exploration flow if needed |
| Find prior work | "has anyone done X before" / "search past work for rate limiting" / "find the previous implementation" | `search` |
| Recall a task playbook | "have we done this before" / "recall how we did X" / "how did we do this last time" | `recall` |
| Replay feature history | "replay <feature>" / "walk me through how X was built" / "show me the journey of Y" | `replay` |
| Teach a repo topic | "teach me <topic>" / "how does <topic> work in this repo" / "give me a lesson on X" | `teach` |
| Understand original intent | "explain this function" / "explain parseConfig" / "what was the intent behind src/auth.ts" | `explain` |
| Generate a dispatch / summary | "summarize recent work" / "generate a dispatch" / "what was accomplished this week" | run `entire dispatch` directly |
| Code review with intent context | "review these changes" / "review this branch" / "audit before merging" | `review` |
| Hand off to another agent | "hand off this session" / "continue in another agent" / "pick up the codex session" | `session-handoff` |
| Convert session to skill | "turn this into a skill" / "make a skill from this session" | `session-to-skill` |
| Link session to other repos | "link session to other repos" / "attach session to the foo repo" | `session-crosslink` |
| General exploration | "understand this module" / "explore how auth works" / "help me understand the codebase" | _(self — see below)_ |

If the scenario clearly maps to a sub-skill, delegate entirely to that skill's
workflow. Do not duplicate their steps here.

## General Exploration Flow

When no specific sub-skill fits — e.g. the user asks to "understand this
module" or "explore how auth works" — use this flow:

1. **Identify key files** in the target area (entry points, main types, core
   functions).

2. **Check for checkpoint coverage** on each key file:

```bash
git log --format='%H %s' -5 -- <file>
```

Look for `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers in the commit bodies:

```bash
git log --format='%H %b' -5 -- <file> | grep -B1 'Entire-Checkpoint:'
```

3. **Read intent for covered commits** — extract the checkpoint ID from the
   trailer, then use JSON output for non-interactive consumption:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <checkpoint-id> --json --no-pager
```

If you only have a commit hash (not a checkpoint ID), use:

```bash
entire checkpoint explain --commit <sha> --no-pager
```

4. **Synthesize**: combine the recorded intent (from checkpoints) with the
   current code structure to build a comprehensive understanding.

5. **Report** your findings, clearly distinguishing:
   - Facts backed by checkpoint transcripts (label as "recorded intent")
   - Observations inferred from code alone (label as "inferred from code")

## AI Agent Usage Notes

When running Entire commands from an agent subprocess:

- **Always pass `--json`** for commands that support it and might prompt
  interactively. `--json` implies non-interactive output.
- **Always pass `--no-pager`** to prevent pager activation in subprocess
  contexts.
- **Always specify `--checkpoint <id>` or `--commit <sha>`** for
  `entire checkpoint explain` — without a locator, the command falls back to an
  interactive picker.

## When No Checkpoints Exist

If the target code predates Entire or has no checkpoint coverage:

1. Say explicitly: "No Entire checkpoint history is available for this code."
2. Proceed with standard code understanding (read source, check git log, trace

3. Label all explanations as "inferred from code — not backed by recorded

4. If the user wants deeper history, suggest `search` with related keywords —

Always make it clear whether your answer comes from:

- **Checkpoint-backed history** — you read the actual session transcript and

- **Code inference** — you analyzed the code structure and are reasoning about

Never present inferred intent as if it were recorded fact. The core value of

**What happens when you paste a DB route**

1. The PWA posts the share text to the Node backend on port 8000. The backend parses it, then forwards the journey to the Python model server on port 8501.
2. The model server does not run the fine-tuned model per request. At startup it loaded the checkpoint's precomputed forecasts for the held-out rows from the `scalar_*.npz` files, plus the 60-day history series and cancellation rates, all into memory.
3. For each leg it matches your train and stations to the closest recorded record and returns that row's stored quantiles. Matching is a dictionary lookup, so the whole call is a few milliseconds.

**Proof it is live, not a fixture**

57	    """Lower-case letters and digits only, so 'S 8', 'S8' and 'S  8' agree."""
58	    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9äöüß]", "", str(value or "").lower())

62	    """Every spelling of a recorded train the app might send."""
63	    keys = {norm(f"{row['train_type']}{row['train_number']}"), norm(row["line_number"])}

67	def leg_keys(leg: dict) -> set[str]:
68	    """The spellings carried by a journey leg."""
69	    keys = {norm(leg.get("trainId"))}
70	    number = leg.get("trainNumber")
71	    if number:

77	def station_match(a, b) -> bool:
78	    """Equal after normalisation, or one contains the other (the share text drops parts of names)."""
79	    a, b = norm(a), norm(b)
80	    return bool(a and b) and (a == b or (min(len(a), len(b)) >= 4 and (a in b or b in a)))

83	def local_naive(value: str) -> pd.Timestamp:
84	    """An ISO timestamp as the naive local time the examples use."""
85	    ts = pd.Timestamp(value)
86	    if ts.tzinfo is None:
87	        return ts
88	    return ts.tz_convert(LOCAL_TZ).tz_localize(None)

91	def train_class(train_id: str) -> str:
92	    """The class the examples use, from the train id alone."""
93	    prefix = re.match(r"[A-Za-z]+", str(train_id or ""))
94	    kind = prefix.group(0).upper() if prefix else ""

102	def probs_from_quantiles(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
103	    """A minute distribution with the given quantiles at :data:`metrics.LEVELS`, mass spread
104	    uniformly between neighbouring quantiles. Used for prediction files that saved no ``probs``."""
105	    q = np.clip(np.round(q).astype(int), 0, MINUTES - 1)
106	    levels = np.concatenate([[0.0], metrics.LEVELS, [1.0]])
107	    edges = np.concatenate([[0], q, [min(MINUTES - 1, q[-1] + max(1, q[-1] - q[-2]) * 2)]])
108	    probs = np.zeros(MINUTES)
109	    for lo, hi, mass in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:], np.diff(levels)):
110	        lo, hi = int(min(lo, hi)), int(max(lo, hi))
111	        probs[lo:hi + 1] += mass / (hi - lo + 1)
112	    return probs / probs.sum()
113

115	def rounded(probs: np.ndarray) -> list[float]:
116	    """Compact JSON: six decimals, still summing to one within float noise."""
117	    return [round(float(p), 6) for p in probs]

120	def short_explanation(text: str) -> str:
121	    """One or two of the model's own sentences for the train card: how late the running train left its
122	    last stop, how the trains before it did today, else how late the target ran in the last hours. The
123	    rationale follows a fixed order, so they are found by their openings; without a match, the first."""
124	    sentences = [s.strip() for s in re.split(r"(?<=\.)\s+(?=[A-Z])", text.strip()) if s.strip()]
125	    running = [s for s in sentences if s.startswith("The train left")]
126	    today = [s for s in sentences if s.startswith(("Today the previous", "No earlier train"))]
127	    recent = [s for s in sentences if re.match(r"At .+ of stops ran", s)]
128	    return " ".join((running + today + recent)[:2] or sentences[:1])

137	class Forecaster:
138	    """Recorded trips, their saved forecasts, and an optional live model."""
139	
140	    def __init__(self, frame: pd.DataFrame, predictions: list[Path] | None = None, model=None,
141	                 mode: str = "both", scaling: str = "z", model_id: str = "db-trip-delay", live=None):
142	        self.frame = frame.reset_index(drop=True)
143	        self.model, self.mode, self.scaling, self.model_id = model, mode, scaling, model_id
144	        self.live = live  # live.Live: examples built from the Timetables API for legs without a record
145	        self.live_cache: dict[str, tuple[float, dict, pd.Series]] = {}
146	        self.live_locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = {}
147	        self.guard, self.model_lock = threading.Lock(), threading.Lock()
148	        self.explanations: dict[str, dict] = {}
149	        arrivals = pd.to_datetime(self.frame["k_arr_pt"])
150	        self.by_minute: dict[pd.Timestamp, list[int]] = {}
151	        for i, ts in enumerate(arrivals.dt.floor("min")):
152	            self.by_minute.setdefault(ts, []).append(i)
153	        self.keys = [train_keys(row) for _, row in self.frame.iterrows()]
154	        self.saved: dict[int, tuple[dict, int]] = {}
155	        for path in predictions or []:
156	            data = np.load(path)
157	            arrays = {k: data[k] for k in data.files}
158	            for j, example_id in enumerate(arrays["example_id"].tolist()):
159	                self.saved.setdefault(int(example_id), (arrays, j))
160	        self.priors = self._priors()
161	
162	    def _priors(self) -> dict[str, tuple[np.ndarray, float]]:
163	        """Empirical delay distributions per train type and per class, for legs without a record."""
164	        priors = {}
165	        for key, group in list(self.frame.groupby("train_type")) + list(self.frame.groupby("cls")):
166	            if len(group) < MIN_PRIOR and key not in set(self.frame["cls"]):
167	                continue
168	            runs = group[~group["cancelled"].astype(bool)]
169	            counts = np.bincount(np.clip(runs["target_minutes"].fillna(0).astype(int), 0, MINUTES - 1), minlength=MINUTES)
170	            priors[str(key)] = (counts / max(1, counts.sum()), float(group["cancelled"].astype(bool).mean()))
171	        return priors
172	
173	    def candidates(self, leg: dict) -> list[int]:
174	        """Rows whose train and planned arrival agree with the leg, station-matched rows first."""
175	        try:
176	            arrival = local_naive(leg["plannedArrival"]).floor("min")
177	        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
178	            return []
179	        wanted = leg_keys(leg)
180	        rows = [i for d in range(-MATCH_MINUTES, MATCH_MINUTES + 1)
181	                for i in self.by_minute.get(arrival + pd.Timedelta(minutes=d), []) if self.keys[i] & wanted]
182	        station = (leg.get("to") or {}).get("name")
183	        with_station = [i for i in rows if station_match(station, self.frame.at[i, "k_station"])]
184	        return with_station or ([] if station and rows and not with_station else rows)
185	
186	    def pick(self, rows: list[int], now: pd.Timestamp | None) -> int:
187	        """The forecast made last before ``now``, or the latest one before the planned arrival."""
188	        frame = self.frame.loc[rows]
189	        if now is not None:
190	            before = frame[pd.to_datetime(frame["t0"]) <= now]
191	            if len(before):
192	                return int(before["t0"].astype(str).idxmax())
193	        lead = frame["lead_minutes"].astype(float)
194	        return int(sorted(rows, key=lambda i: (lead[i] < 0, abs(lead[i])))[0])
195	
196	    def forecast_row(self, i: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, float, str]:
197	        """Minute distribution and P(cancelled) for one recorded trip, and where they came from."""
198	        row = self.frame.loc[i]
199	        saved = self.saved.get(int(row["example_id"]))
200	        if saved is not None:
201	            arrays, j = saved
202	            probs = arrays["probs"][j].astype(np.float64) if "probs" in arrays else probs_from_quantiles(arrays["quantiles"][j])
203	            return probs / probs.sum(), float(arrays["p_cancel"][j]), "saved forecast"
204	        if self.model is not None:
205	            probs, p_cancel = self.model_forecast(row)
206	            return probs, p_cancel, "live model"

**Why it was missing:** your teammates didn't remove anything; the model had nothing to explain for this train.

Your suspicion is right: for this leg the model isn't getting data that means what the reasoning says. I rebuilt EC 199's offline example with the real code:

| Input | Value | What it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| `t0` (when the forecast is "made") | 01:09 tonight | now, not shortly before the 22:23 arrival |
| `lead_minutes` | 1,273 | about 21 h ahead; in training, 99% of examples were at most 375 min ahead (max 829) |
| earlier trains / corridor trains | 0 / 0 | offline mode never fills these, so "No earlier train … reached Buchloe" means "no data" |
| `station_late_3h` | 0.60 (showed as 100% in the earlier run) | stored Sep 11 values for the hours before 01:00 at night, not the hours before your arrival |
| stops behind each hour | 218 / 24 ≈ 9 assumed per hour | even at night, when Buchloe has very few stops |
| history | none | no stored EC 199 run |

In training, a row with 0 earlier trains means there really were none (about 20% of examples), so the model reads the offline row as a quiet station with a late night. The generated reasoning repeats that.

There's also a better way than patching the offline row. DB serves Buchloe's timetable up to about 18 h ahead (19:00 works right now, 22:00 doesn't yet). The only reason your leg goes offline is that Zürich HB isn't in DB's API. When the trip is within that window, the train can be found at its German stops instead: the destination's timetable lists the stations the train called at before it arrives. The forecast could then start from the first German station on the route, such as Lindau or Memmingen. That gives real earlier trains, real station hours and real delays once the train is running, and no "Offline estimate" label. Your actual screenshot, taken on the train, is exactly that case.

What I need to build it, all independent:
1. `live.py` lines 60–300: constants, `stop_row` (which fields a stop carries, e.g. the stations before and after), `row_keys`/`leg_keys` and `Feeds.station`/`stops`.
2. **Real DB data:** today's EC/ECE arrivals at Buchloe within the window. I need how DB names these trains (EC or ECE, and number), their arrival times, and whether the list of earlier stations starts at Zürich HB. That also gives me a real train to test with.
3. `prompts.py` lines 89–175: exactly how the rationale words missing data, for the trips beyond the 18 h window that will stay offline.

content.text:
The live data answers the design question. At Buchloe, DB lists the Zürich–Munich trains as **ECE**, every two hours: ECE 95 at 08:23, 97, 99, 191, 193, then ECE 195 at 18:23. Their earlier stations are only `Lindau-Reutin | Memmingen`. EC 199 follows the same pattern, as ECE 199 arriving 22:23. That means two things block live data for your leg:
1. **Zürich HB isn't in DB's API.** The live example can't find the train at its boarding station.
2. **The names differ.** Your share says "EC 199" and DB says "ECE 199", so even at German stations the train-name match (`row_keys & leg_keys`) fails.

`prompts.py` confirms the reasoning problem. The sentences "No earlier train … in the last 6 hours" and "…% of stops ran late in the last 3 hours" are written unconditionally. An offline row states missing data as fact, and the model reads it that way.

**Plan:**
- **Name matching:** a `same_train` helper also accepts the same train number under a sibling type (EC↔ECE, IC↔ICE). The live example uses it when matching the train at a station.
- **Starting outside Germany:** when the boarding station isn't in DB's API at all, a new `_entry_stop` finds the train at the destination at its planned arrival. From the stations DB lists before it, it takes the first one the API knows (Lindau-Reutin) and finds the same run there. The live example then builds from that stop as usual, with real earlier trains, station hours and delays. A source line says "Zürich HB is outside DB's live timetable, so live data starts at Lindau-Reutin".
- **German boarding stations:** they keep the current behaviour, so a wrong departure time isn't silently replaced by the run's origin.
- **Trips more than ~18 h ahead:** they stay offline. I'll report that case and ask about it separately rather than guess.

What I need now, all independent:
1. Add `same_train` to `live.py` next to `leg_keys`.
2. Rework the start of `Live.example` and add `_entry_stop`.
3. Add the "outside DB's live timetable" source line in `example`.
4. Read `test_live.py`'s fixtures to see whether a focused test for this path is cheap to add.
